title: Observable error handling: fix InvalidAccessError + visible extensible log
description:
P0 UX for error handling. Two linked symptoms when the host/browser session misbehaves:

1) Uncaught console error (noise we must stop emitting):
   Uncaught InvalidAccessError: Failed to execute "close" on "WebSocket": The close code must be either 1000, or between 3000 and 4999. 1008 is neither.
   at Fv.protocolFailure (index-BeaCCIy4.js:9:152606)
   at d.onmessage (index-BeaCCIy4.js:9:148240)
   ROOT CAUSE: apps/web/src/session/websocket-transport.ts protocolFailure() calls this.socket?.close(1008, "invalid host conversation protocol"). Browser WebSocket API only permits CLIENT-initiated close codes 1000 or 3000-4999; 1008 is server-only, so close() throws InvalidAccessError (uncaught, since protocolFailure runs inside onmessage). index-BeaCCIy4.js is the apps/web Vite bundle. Host mirror: apps/host/src/sidecar/AudioClient.ts protocolFailure() closes with 1008 and the sidecar.failure handler with 1011; node ws permits these so no throw, but keep codes spec-conformant anyway.

2) Opaque UI alert "The host sent invalid conversation data. Local playback was stopped.":
   Emitted by notifyFailure() in apps/web/src/session/websocket-transport.ts whenever the strict host-event validator or sequence check rejects a message (see isStrictHostEvent + handleBinary checks). The message names no reason (which event, which check, what was expected vs received), so a user cannot diagnose or paste actionable context.

REQUESTED UX:
- An extensible, always-visible activity/error log (ring buffer) that records session events, transport events, validation failures with detail (event type, expected vs actual), state changes, and errors; rendered in a collapsible UI panel with a one-click copy so the user can paste it to an agent.
- Replace the uncaught InvalidAccessError with a valid close code (3000-4999, e.g. 4000) or close(1000)/terminate; route error visibility through the log instead of raw console.error spam.

RESOLUTION (decided approach; not yet implemented):

1. Fix the InvalidAccessError (browser):
   apps/web/src/session/websocket-transport.ts protocolFailure() must not close with 1008. Use a private application code from 3000-4999, e.g. close(4000, "invalid host conversation protocol"), or close(1000) with the reason string. Guard the close (check readyState === OPEN, wrap in try/catch) so no exception can escape onmessage and hit the console as an uncaught error. Same shape fix for the host mirror: apps/host/src/sidecar/AudioClient.ts protocolFailure() close(1008) -> 4001, and the sidecar.failure handler close(1011) -> 4002 (node ws happens to accept 1008/1011, but they are server-only codes by spec; keep the client spec-conformant for symmetry).

2. Make the failure alert diagnostic:
   Thread a reason from each protocolFailure() call site (which event type, which check failed, expected vs received) into notifyFailure(). The UI alert must name the failing event/check instead of the generic "The host sent invalid conversation data. Local playback was stopped."

3. Visible extensible log:
   - New module (e.g. apps/web/src/session/activity-log.ts): typed ring buffer (cap ~500 entries), entry = { ts, level: info|warn|error, source, message, detail? }, append()/clear() API, subscribe() for rendering, and a toText()/toJSON() for copying.
   - Wire it into websocket-transport.ts (open/close/protocol failures with diagnostics), controller.ts (degrade/terminalize/failure events), and state transitions.
   - UI: collapsible "Activity log" panel in SessionScreen.tsx, level badges, copy-to-clipboard button (navigator.clipboard.writeText(log.toText())).
   - Error paths must never throw into the console; console mirror via console.debug only.

4. Verification:
   - Tamper a host event (bad payload/sequence) and assert: no InvalidAccessError in the browser console, alert shows the failing check, log panel contains the entry, copy works.
   - Host: run sidecar protocol violation and assert no RangeError/TypeError and sidecar sees a 3000-4999 close code.

ACCEPTANCE:
- No InvalidAccessError on protocol failure in browser console.
- UI alert on protocol failure includes diagnostics (which event/check failed), and the same detail lands in the copyable log.
- Log is extensible (typed add/append API) and rendered + copyable in the web UI.
- Host sidecar client close codes fixed for spec compliance.

pi_tasks.validation: transport close 4000 guarded (no InvalidAccessError, unit-proven); diagnostics threaded to alert; activity-log ring buffer + copyable UI panel; host client codes 4001/4002 spec-conformant; web=104 host=221 check passed; e2e 4/5, readiness failure pre-existing on clean HEAD

title: Strip custom styling to shadcn defaults so any theme/accent permeates the app
description:
Goal: keep the web UI as close to stock shadcn (new-york, base-ui base per components.json) as possible so dropping any shadcn theme or accent into the token block re-skins the whole app consistently. Custom styling only where absolutely necessary (domain-specific chat primitives, layout that utilities can't express).

Audit and reduce:
1. globals.css: the :root token block + @theme inline mapping is the intended theme hook, keep. Everything else (shimmer keyframes, reduced-motion override, stray rules) must justify itself or move into a component using stock patterns.
2. session.css (53 lines) and readiness.css (18 lines): migrate bespoke classes onto tailwind utilities / shadcn component props in the TSX. Keep plain CSS only for layout that is genuinely awkward as utilities (conversation scroller sizing, activity-log grid). No hardcoded hex anywhere outside the token block; color-mix() on token vars is acceptable.
3. ui components vs registry defaults: button.tsx (custom min-h-11 sizes, variant set), badge.tsx (custom primary/success/warning variants), card.tsx (stripped down), alert.tsx, spinner.tsx, switch.tsx, tooltip.tsx, scroll-area.tsx, button-group.tsx. Align each with the shadcn registry source adapted to base-ui; document intentional deviations (e.g. 44px touch targets) instead of silent forks.
4. Domain primitives bubble.tsx / marker.tsx / message.tsx / message-scroller.tsx have no shadcn equivalent, keep them, but they must style exclusively via tokens + utilities so themes permeate.
5. Delete dead CSS/classes as screens get migrated (e.g. .readiness-list, .success, .error, old .secondary/.danger leftovers if any).

Acceptance:
- Replace the :root token block with a stock shadcn theme (e.g. default zinc or any theme from ui.shadcn.com/themes) and every surface (readiness, session, recording controls, activity log) renders on-theme with no leftover off-palette hex, borders, or shadows.
- rg for hex colors outside the token block returns nothing.
- pnpm typecheck + test in apps/web and root playwright e2e pass.

Coordinate with pending hr7 (session screen polish) and tm5 (readiness rebuild): run after them or absorb their styling decisions to avoid rework.

title: Give the persona a unique character: fake lived experiences and tastes to quote from
description:
A good podcaster regularly weaves in their own tastes and experiences; ours currently cannot. The default persona (packages/contracts/src/persona/defaults.ts) is a blank slate: name 'Thoughtful companion', one interest ('systems thinking'), body 'Be concise, curious, and respectful.' Give the agent a distinct, consistent character it can draw on in responses.

Current plumbing (for grounding):
- Persona schema: ln.json in packages/contracts (generated into TS + python): name, invitation_only, posture_weights, challenge_enabled, interests (max 20 x 80 chars), body markdown (16KB).
- Host: SessionOrchestrator.ts parsePersona(options.personaSource ?? DEFAULT_PERSONA_MARKDOWN); boundedPersonaForPi() serializes name/weights/interests/body into the Pi prompt; PiClient.ts builds 'Return only the response text, at most 45 words. Posture: ... Persona interpretation: ...'.
- Web UI already displays the assistant as 'Oliver' while the persona name says 'Thoughtful companion'; align them.

Work:
1. Character content: write a default persona 'Oliver' with a small set of fake lived experiences and concrete preferences to quote from (e.g. a formative stint volunteering at a night radio show, growing up near the sea, tastes like field recordings, analog photography, slow cooking, chess endgames). Specific enough to feel real, broad enough to connect to many topics.
2. Representation: decide between encoding experiences/tastes in the body markdown vs extending the ln.json schema with structured fields (e.g. experiences: string[] mirroring interests constraints). Structured fields make them validated, easy to edit, and explicitly passed to Pi; schema change requires regenerating contracts and updating validation tests in TS and python (packages/contracts/test/persona.test.ts, services/audio/tests/test_contracts.py). Prefer structured if the regen cost is small, body markdown otherwise.
3. Prompt guidance: in the Pi prompt, instruct the model to bring in a taste or experience the way a podcaster does: only when it genuinely illuminates the user's topic, at most one per response, lightly (never a life story), stay within the 45-word budget, and never invent experiences beyond the provided list.
4. Consistency: persona name should match the displayed name 'Oliver' in apps/web conversation rows and the shimmer marker.

Validation: contracts + host + web unit tests pass, python contract tests pass if schema changed, and a manual transcript/session vibe check that responses occasionally and naturally reference the character without derailing the user.

title: Voice session drops connection and degrades mid-conversation
description: During a live voice session the transport connection was lost after ~2 minutes of normal operation (states cycling listening/deciding/reasoning/speaking fine, then at 01:07:33 response failed during 'speaking', playback stopped as failed, transport reported 'session connection lost', mic capture stopped). User reports this happened while they paused for a while, but idle/pause should not kill the session. Investigate transport resilience: reconnection, keepalive/heartbeat, and recovery of response playback instead of hard-degrading the session.

title: Stream assistant text into the UI before audio via reasoning.delta, dim-to-solid like user transcripts
description:
Perceived response latency: today the assistant row only appears when reasoning.final lands, right before TTS audio starts, so the user stares at 'Forming a response…' the whole time. The response text is available much earlier (Pi streams text deltas; host forwards them to TTS), and the user-side transcript already has a beloved effect we should mirror: tentative text streams in dimmed/desaturated and materializes to full saturation once final.

Current plumbing (grounding):
- Protocol: reasoning.delta is already in the core-events enum (events/core-events.json), but nobody emits or consumes it.
- Host: apps/host/src/session/SessionOrchestrator.ts (~line 305) consumes PiClient deltas ({type:'delta'}) and appends assembler chunks to the TTS speechStream only; nothing is sent to the browser until reasoning.final.
- Web: apps/web/src/session/state.ts reduces reasoning.started (dominant 'reasoning', shimmer 'Oliver is typing…') and reasoning.final (creates the assistant conversationItem); tentativeText + .tentative class (dashed border, opacity .7 in session.css) is the user-side streaming pattern to mirror.

Work:
1. Host: emit reasoning.delta envelopes to the browser from the delta loop (per assembler chunk or lightly coalesced, e.g. every ~50-100ms or N chars), carrying responseId/turnId/epoch and cumulative or incremental text; respect cancellation/epoch switches and don't emit after reasoning.final.
2. Web state: accumulate deltas into a tentative assistant text keyed by responseId; clear on reasoning.final (which materializes the stable row), response.failed, turn.cancel, and epoch bumps.
3. Web UI: while deltas flow, render the assistant row early with the text in the dimmed/tentative style (reuse or generalize the .tentative effect: dimmed -> fully saturated on materialize); keep the shimmer only until the first delta arrives. Auto-scroll must keep working (MessageScroller anchoring with a growing row).
4. Keep the 45-word budget and validation where they are (host-side); deltas are purely presentational, final text remains authoritative.

Validation: unit tests in state.test.ts/controller.test.ts for delta accumulation + materialization + cancellation; e2e extension emitting reasoning.delta and asserting the dimmed row appears before tts.started and solidifies on reasoning.final; manual check that perceived wait drops noticeably.
